overall.summary: Nothing is refuted: coverage, function preservation, closed forms and almost every number reproduce, and each part's reading holds under probing. Three small weakenings: the age-part AUC is double-rounded (0.851 stated, 0.850 true), 'lower income raises risk for everyone' has 9 training exceptions, and 'visits has the largest effect of the four' holds only for the typical case (over the data, noise moves predictions most).

age_risk.why: Its contribution rises with age on 95% of training rows and falls on none, carrying most of the model's age effect outside urban smokers.

urban_smoker_age_gate.why: It steepens the age effect for urban smokers (age slope 1.89 logit per 10 years vs 0.27 or less elsewhere), but it also acts on most urban non-smokers and some rural smokers, so the name covers only part of its behaviour.

female_bmi.why: Higher bmi raises women's predicted risk on every row (+0.76 logit per 2 bmi) and men's hardly at all in the usual range, which the observed rates match; the heavy-men rise is a stated side effect.

low_income.why: The unit adds risk that falls with income on every row it acts on (off above about 80 thousand) and grows with age, which reads as a low-income risk factor.
